This project is being built under **CodeYatraNP** as a collaborative learning and impact platform for young developers, designers, and thinkers. --- ## ✨ Vision Most people set goals. name: Nidaan
readme:
# Nidaan

AI-powered medical intelligence platform. Free, open source, 13 languages. No sign-up, no tracking, no ads.

## What is this

Nidaan is a medical AI web application that provides:

- **AI Consultation** — Chat with a fine-tuned medical LLM grounded in WHO, CDC, and NHS guidelines
- **Image Analysis** — Upload medical images (X-rays, scans) for AI-assisted diagnostics
- **Blood Analytics** — Generate 12 visualizations from blood test datasets (organ panels, correlation heatmaps, anomaly detection, risk scores, PCA clustering)
- **Voice Input** — Speak your symptoms in any of 13 supported languages via Web Speech API + Whisper fallback
- **Health Tracking** — Medications, vitals, appointments, EHR export

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Frontend | Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript |
| Styling | Vanilla CSS, Hanken Grotesk, Material Symbols |
| Animation | GSAP (ScrollTrigger, clip-path reveals, text scramble) |
| Auth | NextAuth.js v5 with Google OAuth |
| Voice | Web Speech API (primary) + Whisper via HuggingFace (fallback) |
| State | React hooks + localStorage (sessions, patient data, preferences) |
| Analytics Backend | Python Flask API, matplotlib, plotly, scikit-learn, seaborn |
| Design System | Obsidian Mono (extreme minimalism, black/white, sharp edges) |

## Project Structure

```
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── page.tsx                 # Landing page (HoverGrid animations)
│   │   ├── login/page.tsx           # Google OAuth login
│   │   ├── chat/page.tsx            # Dashboard (Consult, Imaging, Analytics)
│   │   └── api/
│   │       ├── auth/[...nextauth]/  # NextAuth Google provider
│   │       └── voice/transcribe/    # Whisper transcription proxy
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── HoverGrid.tsx            # Landing with GSAP scroll animations
│   │   ├── AboutSection.tsx         # Scroll snap section with text scramble
│   │   ├── TextScramble.tsx         # Animated text reveal component
│   │   └── dashboard/
│   │       ├── Sidebar.tsx          # Collapsible session list (resizable)
│   │       ├── ChatTab.tsx          # Consult chat with voice input
│   │       ├── ImageAnalysisTab.tsx # Split view (resizable) + chat
│   │       ├── AnalyticsTab.tsx     # Python backend integration
│   │       ├── PatientIntake.tsx    # Patient info modal (name, age, gender)
│   │       └── Waveform.tsx         # Audio frequency visualizer
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   ├── useSessions.ts           # Session CRUD + localStorage
│   │   └── useVoiceInput.ts         # Dual voice engine hook
│   └── auth.ts                      # NextAuth configuration
├── backend/
│   └── server.py                    # Flask API for blood analytics
├── nidaan_blood_analytics.py        # Python data pipeline (2000 patients, 12 viz)
└── public/media/                    # Images, videos, backgrounds
```

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- Python 3.10+ (for analytics backend)
- Google Cloud Console OAuth credentials

### 1. Clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Gun4shot/Nidaan.git
cd Nidaan
```

### 2. Install Frontend

```bash
npm install
```

### 3. Install Python Dependencies

```bash
pip install flask flask-cors numpy pandas matplotlib seaborn plotly scikit-learn scipy networkx kaleido
```

### 4. Environment Variables

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

Fill in:

```
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-google-client-id
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-google-client-secret
NEXTAUTH_SECRET=run-openssl-rand-base64-32
NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=hf_your_token_here
```

**Google OAuth setup:**
1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials
2. Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application)
3. Set Authorized redirect URI: `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`

**HuggingFace token (for voice fallback):**
1. Go to https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens
2. Create a free Read token

### 5. Run

```bash
# Terminal 1 — Frontend
npm run dev

# Terminal 2 — Analytics backend (optional)
python backend/server.py
```

Open http://localhost:3000

## Features

### Landing Page
- GSAP scroll animations with clip-path image reveals
- Scroll snap sections (landing, about, footer)
- Background video crossfade on scroll
- Text scramble animation on about section
- Film grain overlay

### Dashboard
- **3 tabs**: Consult, Imaging, Analytics
- **Tab switcher** with sliding pill indicator
- **Dark mode** toggle (persisted in localStorage)
- **Collapsible sidebar** with resizable width
- **Session management**: create, rename (right-click), delete
- **Patient intake modal**: name, age, gender on new session
- **Settings panel**: language, voice input, notifications
- **Profile panel**: Google account info, sign out

### Consult Tab
- Chat interface with message bubbles
- Voice input (real-time transcription, words appear as you speak)
- Copy button on message hover
- Welcome message personalized with patient name

### Imaging Tab
- 50/50 resizable split (drag handle between panels)
- Image upload with thumbnail strip
- 3 view modes: Single, Grid, Compare
- Zoom controls
- Image removal (toolbar button + thumbnail X button)
- Voice input on the chat panel
- Copy button on messages

### Analytics Tab
- Upload CSV dataset or load existing
- Python backend generates 12 visualizations:
  - Organ Panel Summary
  - Reference Range Bars
  - Correlation Heatmap
  - Distribution Plots (violin + KDE)
  - Patient Radar Chart
  - Trend Lines Over Time
  - Anomaly Detection (Isolation Forest)
  - Composite Risk Score Gauge
  - PCA Clustering
  - Population Percentile Rank
  - What-If Simulator
  - Biomarker Causal Graph (DAG)
- Download individual PNGs or all as ZIP
- Download dataset CSV
- State persists across tab switches

### Voice Input
- **Web Speech API**: browser-native, real-time interim transcription
- **Whisper fallback**: HuggingFace free inference API for unsupported browsers/languages
- Waveform visualization during recording
- Works on both Consult and Imaging tabs

## Design System

Obsidian Mono — extreme minimalism:

- **Colors**: `#000000` background, `#ffffff` foreground, `#808080` muted
- **Font**: Hanken Grotesk (all weights)
- **Icons**: Material Symbols Outlined
- **Corners**: Sharp (0px), no shadows, flat layering
- **Labels**: 11px, 600 weight, 0.15em letter-spacing, uppercase
- **Dark mode**: `#121414` background, `#e3e2e2` text, full component coverage

## License

Apache 2.0 — use it, mo

name: Sentinal-1-SAR-framework
readme:
# Sentinel-1 SAR Framework for Road Vulnerability Assessment in Nepal

This repository contains the final manuscript, the Jupyter notebooks used for analysis and figure generation, publication figures, and the supporting road-network and slope raster inputs.

## Contents

- `paper/` - final submitted manuscript.
- `notebooks/` - analysis notebooks used for seasonal backscatter, risk classification, and figures.
- `figures/` - high-resolution figures reported in the manuscript.
- `data/geospatial/` - road shapefile components and slope rasters for Gajuri, Sindhuli, Guthitar, Simaltal-Bharatpur, and Daklang-Listi.
- `requirements.txt` - Python package dependencies used by the notebooks.

## Notebook order

1. `research.ipynb` - cross-site seasonal backscatter analysis.
2. `temporalbackscatter.ipynb` - temporal backscatter visualisation.
3. `researchfig3.ipynb` - statistical comparison figure workflow.
4. `risk_classification.ipynb` - hydrological sensitivity, anomaly detection, and validation maps.

## Raw Sentinel-1 time-series data

The analysis uses site-level aligned backscatter CSV files. They are intentionally not committed because they are large (about 1.2 GB total; several individual files exceed GitHub's 100 MB file limit). The filenames needed by the notebooks are listed in [data/RAW_BACKSCATTER_CSVS_REQUIRED.md](data/RAW_BACKSCATTER_CSVS_REQUIRED.md).

The notebooks preserve the original Google Drive paths used for the analysis. Before rerunning locally, update those paths to the location where the raw CSV files are stored. The committed shapefiles and slope rasters are provided under `data/geospatial/`.

## Paper

The final manuscript is [SAR_Road_Vulnerability_Nepal_final.docx](paper/SAR_Road_Vulnerability_Nepal_final.docx).

name: SolveScript
readme:
# SolveScript

SolveScript is a study studio for Cambridge International AS & A Level paper practice. It supports Paper 1 multiple-choice sessions and full written-paper sessions with PDF annotation, timers, reports, and progress tracking.

**Live website:** [solvescript.onrender.com](https://solvescript.onrender.com/)

SolveScript is free and open source. Students can organise past papers, annotate each page independently, take timed exams, save their work, and optionally bring their own Gemini API key for AI-assisted written-answer review.

## What students can do

- Browse the public Paper 1 library, filter by subject, year, session, and difficulty, and practise as a guest.
- Work in casual mode with immediate answer feedback or timed exam mode with feedback held until submission.
- Annotate PDFs with drawing, highlighting, shapes, text, undo/redo, and clear controls.
- Upload a question paper and marking scheme. Signed-in uploads are parsed and saved; guest uploads remain only for the current browser session.
- Take written papers when signed in, save drafts, compare annotated work with the official scheme, and record a self-mark.

## Local development

Requirements: Node.js 18+ and MongoDB (local or Atlas) for account-backed features. The public libraries have a local fallback for development.

```powershell
# Terminal 1: API
cd server
npm install
Copy-Item .env.example .env
npm run dev

# Terminal 2: client, from the repository root
npm install
npm run dev
```

The client runs at `http://127.0.0.1:5173` and the API at `http://127.0.0.1:5000` by default.

## Configuration and security

Copy [`server/.env.example`](server/.env.example) and supply your own values. Do not commit `.env` files, MongoDB URIs, OAuth secrets, API keys, or JWT secrets.

For production:

- Set distinct `JWT_SECRET` and `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` values of at least 32 random characters. The server refuses placeholder or short values in production.
- Rotate any credential that has ever been committed or shared outside the deployment secret store.
- Set `CLIENT_URL` to the exact HTTPS client origin and configure the matching Google OAuth callback URL if Google sign-in is enabled.
- Keep uploaded files on trusted storage and enforce HTTPS. Authentication tokens are HTTP-only cookies and are never included in API JSON responses.

## Verification

```powershell
npm run lint
npm run build
node --test server/tests/localPaperLibrary.test.cjs server/tests/ingestCaieWrittenPapers.test.cjs server/tests/writtenPaperSpecs.test.cjs src/pages/Solver/attemptReport.test.js
```

## Stack

React 19, Vite, React Router, Fabric.js, React-PDF, Express, MongoDB/Mongoose, JWT cookies, Multer, and pdf-parse.

name: Whitebook
readme:
# WhiteBook — Digital SAT Practice

A pixel-perfect, College Board Bluebook–style SAT Reading & Writing practice platform built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS v4.

## Features

- **Authentic Bluebook UI** — Top bar with timer, directions, highlights/notes, review panel, more menu; diagonal rainbow accent bars; bottom bar with question counter and navigation
- **Two-column split layout** — Passage on left, question + choices on right (with vertical divider)
- **Multiple sessions** — Run several practice tests in parallel; each saved independently in localStorage
- **Dashboard with stats** — Circular accuracy pie chart, total tests, questions solved, answers checked, accuracy
- **Timed & untimed modes** — 85 seconds per question (configurable), with color-coded timer (green → yellow → red)
- **Full keyboard support** — `A/B/C/D` to select, `Enter` next, `Shift+Enter` previous, `Space` flag, `Ctrl+C` check, `Shift+H` highlight mode, `Esc` to exit
- **Highlight & Notes** — Select text in passage/question to highlight in yellow/pink/green; Shift-click or right-click to remove; scoped per session
- **Eliminate choices** — Click X on any choice to strike it out; click again to restore
- **Mark for review** — Flag questions with a bookmark icon; shows in review panel
- **Change & re-check** — After checking, pick a different answer and check again
- **Explanation modal** — View correct answer, your answer, and full rationale
- **Results page** — Hollow pie accuracy chart, per-question drill-down with expandable details, time tracking, filter by status
- **Session persistence** — Auto-saves to localStorage; resume on reload; multiple named sessions
- **Responsive & accessible** — Rounded cards, smooth animations (fade, slide, pop), prefers-reduced-motion support

## Tech Stack

- **React 19** + **TypeScript**
- **Vite** for dev & build
- **Tailwind CSS v4** (via PostCSS)
- **React Router v6**
- **Oxlint** for linting

## Getting Started

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start dev server
npm run dev

# Build for production
npm run build

# Preview production build
npm run preview

# Lint
npm run lint
```

## Deploy to Render

1. Push this repo to GitHub
2. In Render dashboard, create a **New Static Site**
3. Connect your GitHub repo
4. Settings:
   - **Build Command**: `npm install && npm run build`
   - **Publish Directory**: `dist`
5. Or use the included `render.yaml` for IaC deploy

### Environment Variables

No environment variables required — all data is stored in browser localStorage.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `A` `B` `C` `D` | Select answer choice |
| `Enter` | Next question |
| `Shift` + `Enter` | Previous question |
| `←` / `→` | Navigate |
| `Space` | Toggle flag (mark for review) |
| `Ctrl` + `C` | Check answer |
| `Shift` + `H` | Toggle highlight mode |
| `Esc` | Exit highlight mode / close modals |
| `Shift` + click highlight | Remove highlight |
| Right-click highlight | Remove highlight |

## Data

150 official-style SAT Reading & Writing questions sourced from College Board materials, organized by:
- **4 Domains**: Information and Ideas, Craft and Structure, Expression of Ideas, Standard English
- **9 Skills**: Central Ideas, Command of Evidence, Inferences, Cross-Text Connections, Text Structure, Words in Context, Rhetorical Synthesis, Transitions, Conventions (Boundaries / Form & Sense)
- **3 Difficulties**: Easy, Medium, Hard
